\section[a mentira]{a mentira — a lie}

\label{lesson:PT-C192-mentira}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for a mother-in-law, then the Portuguese for a father-in-law.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a mentira}
\textbf{a mentira} — \textquotedblleft{}a lie\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{mentira} is built from the verb \textquotedblleft{}to lie\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1), which $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{mentiri}, \textquotedblleft{}to lie\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[a regra]{a regra — a rule}

\label{lesson:PT-C192-regra}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a regra}
\textbf{a regra} — \textquotedblleft{}a rule\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{regra} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{regula}, \textquotedblleft{}ruler, rule\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1), from \emph{regere}, \textquotedblleft{}to guide\textquotedblright{} — inherited. \emph{regula} lost a vowel and its \emph{-l-} became \emph{-r-}.
\end{cousinweb}
